newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says not planning cargo rate increase.
newsitem.headline: SAS says not planning cargo rate increase.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) on Wednesday said it had no plans to raise freight rates despite a 2.5 percent lift in its Scandinavia-Britain passenger fares in the wake of a similar move by British Airways.
Earlier this month SAS said it would raise ticket prices between Scandinavia and Britain after British Airways said higher jet fuel prices had forced it to do so.
"There are two different business areas that rest on two different business logics," SAS Cargo spokesman Robert Skoog told Reuters.
"We are, of course, aware of the effect of rising fuel costs, but we have not decided either way if this will have an effect on cargo rates."

Jet fuel on the European spot market has risen by 30 percent since mid-July as world oil prices rocketed on a bullish combination of Middle East tension, low stocks and strong demand in the approach to winter.
SAS is partially owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
